findings.claim: Token expiration is evaluated by local wall-clock fields instead of absolute instants, so tokens can remain accepted after expiration or be rejected while still valid when the inputs use different UTC offsets.
evidence: evals/cases/case_10/src/tokens.py:5-8 explicitly removes tzinfo from both inputs with replace(tzinfo=None) and then compares the resulting naive local times; replace does not convert either timestamp to a common timezone.
Runtime reproduction: expires_at=2026-08-28T12:05:00+00:00 and now=2026-08-28T09:06:00-03:00 represent now one minute after expiry, but is_token_expired returned false, allowing an expired token.
Runtime reproduction: expires_at=2026-08-28T09:05:00-03:00 and now=2026-08-28T12:00:00+00:00 represent now five minutes before expiry, but is_token_expired returned true, rejecting a valid token.
evals/cases/case_10/tests/test_tokens.py:6-10 covers only two UTC datetimes, so the passing test does not exercise the documented different-zone behavior.
